Using it with a currency that has no rate is an error, and using it with the base currency shows the usual amounts.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

# kitty

Keeps track of shared trip costs: who paid, who owes whom, and how to settle up.
It needs nothing installed except Python 3. Run it from the folder that contains
the `kitty` folder (or set `PYTHONPATH` to that folder). The data lives in a file
called `kitty.json` in the folder you run it from.

Every command starts with `python3 -m kitty`. If something is wrong you get one
line starting with `error:` and nothing is changed.

| What you want | Example |
|---|---|
| Start a new kitty (main currency) | `python3 -m kitty init EUR` |
| Add a person | `python3 -m kitty member add Alice` |
| Remove a person (only if unused) | `python3 -m kitty member remove Alice` |
| List people | `python3 -m kitty member list` |
| Set an exchange rate (1 USD = 0.92 EUR) | `python3 -m kitty rate set USD 0.92` |
| Add an expense (split among everyone) | `python3 -m kitty expense add Alice 45 Dinner --currency USD --date 2026-07-14 --category food` |
| Split among some people | `python3 -m kitty expense add Alice 30 Taxi --among Alice,Bob` |
| Split by exact amounts | `python3 -m kitty expense add Alice 50 Hotel --exact Alice=30,Bob=20` |
| Split by shares | `python3 -m kitty expense add Alice 60 Food --shares Alice=2,Bob=1` |
| Split by percent | `python3 -m kitty expense add Alice 100 Tickets --percent Alice=60,Bob=40` |
| List expenses | `python3 -m kitty expense list` |
| Remove an expense | `python3 -m kitty expense remove 1` |
| Record a payback | `python3 -m kitty payment add Bob Alice 20.70` |
| Who is owed / owes what | `python3 -m kitty balances` |
| Who should pay whom | `python3 -m kitty settle` |
| One person's history | `python3 -m kitty history Bob` |
| Spending by category | `python3 -m kitty report` |
| Save a spreadsheet file | `python3 -m kitty export trip.csv` |

Amounts are positive numbers with at most two decimals. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`
(default: today). Names are not case-sensitive.

Options such as `--currency` go before or after the description, not in the
middle of it. If you give the same option twice, the last one wins.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

# Kitty: shared trip-cost tracker — design

Date: 2026-11-17
Status: draft for approval

## Intent and why

A group of friends on a trip need to record who paid for what, so that at
the end they know who owes whom and how to even up with as few paybacks as
possible. The owner is not a programmer; their friend Sam writes scripts
and will hook the tool up to a spreadsheet. So the tool is a command-line
program whose reports are machine-readable JSON in exactly the format
below, and which never crashes on bad input: it explains the problem and
stops.

## Goals

- Track members, expenses (with flexible splits and foreign currencies),
  payments between members, and exchange rates.
- Report balances, a settlement plan, per-person history, a per-category
  spending report, and a CSV export.
- Exact money math: shares of an expense always add up to it to the cent.

## Non-goals

- No GUI, no web, no multi-user sync, no editing of an existing expense
  (remove and re-add instead), no automatic exchange-rate lookup.

## Anti-goals (would be a failure even if it "works")

- Needs anything installed beyond the Mac's Python 3.9.6.
- A refused command changes `kitty.json` in any way, or a crash leaves it
  half-written.
- A Python traceback shown to the user for bad input.
- Balances that drift by a cent, or shares that don't sum to the expense.
- Past expenses silently changing when the group or a rate changes.

## Constraints

- Run as `python3 -m kitty <command> ...` from the folder that contains the
  `kitty` package. Python 3.9.6, standard library only (so no `match`, no
  `X | Y` type unions at runtime, `date.fromisoformat` is limited, etc.).
- State lives in `kitty.json` in the **current working directory**.
- Success: exit status 0. Any refusal: one line `error: <message>` on
  stderr, nothing on stdout, exit status 1, `kitty.json` byte-for-byte
  unchanged. This includes command-line usage mistakes (unknown command,
  missing argument, unknown option) — argparse's default exit status 2 must
  be overridden to 1 with the same `error:` format.

## Approaches considered

1. **Plain Python package, stdlib only, JSON file state** — chosen.
   `decimal` for money, `json`, `csv`, `argparse`. Matches every constraint.
2. **SQLite database for state** — rejected: Sam asked for `kitty.json`, and
   a plain JSON file is easier for his scripts.
3. **Third-party libraries (e.g. click, a money library) or another
   language** — rejected: violates "nothing to install" and
   `python3 -m kitty`.

The owner agreed to approach 1.

## Commands and output

All JSON output is printed with Python's default `json.dumps` separators
(`", "` and `": "`), on one line, as in the examples. Money is always a
string with exactly two decimals. Money is in the main (base) currency,
except an expense's own `amount`. Object key order is significant and is
given below.

| Command | Prints on success |
|---|---|
| `init CUR` | nothing |
| `member add NAME` / `member remove NAME` | nothing |
| `member list` | `["Alice", "Bob"]` — join order |
| `expense add PAYER AMOUNT DESCRIPTION [opts]` | the new ID, e.g. `1` |
| `expense list` | list of expense objects, by ID |
| `expense remove ID` | nothing |
| `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT [--currency C] [--date D]` | nothing |
| `rate set CUR RATE` | nothing |
| `balances` | object, members in join order |
| `settle` | list of payments, in the order computed |
| `history NAME` | list of entries |
| `report` | object of objects |
| `export FILE` | nothing (writes the CSV) |

Examples (from Sam):

- `expense list`: `[{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner", "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food", "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}]`
- `balances`: `{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}`
- `settle`: `[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]`
- `history Bob`: `[{"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}]`
- `report`: `{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}`

Empty results print `[]` or `{}`.

## Rules decided with the owner

### Kitty and state
- `init CUR` creates `kitty.json` with CUR as the main currency. Refused if
  `kitty.json` already exists. Every other command is refused if it doesn't.
- Anything that changes state is fully validated first; the file is saved
  only on success, by writing a temp file in the same folder and
  `os.replace`-ing it over `kitty.json`.

### Members
- Names are case-insensitive for matching everywhere (in every command and
  option), but always displayed as first added. Adding a name that matches
  an existing one case-insensitively is refused.
- Names may not contain `,` or `=`. (Builder's call: also refuse empty or
  all-whitespace names; strip surrounding whitespace.)
- `member remove` is refused if the person appears in any expense (as payer
  or in its shares) or any payment (as sender or receiver). Otherwise it
  succeeds. Unknown name is refused.

### Expenses
- PAYER must be a member. The payer need not be among the people sharing.
- "Everyone" (no split option) means the members at the moment the expense
  is added; the computed shares are stored with the expense and never
  recomputed. Later joiners are not included in earlier expenses.
- At most one of `--among`, `--exact`, `--shares`, `--percent`.
- `--among A,B`: equal split among those named.
- `--exact A=30,B=20`: amounts in the expense's own currency; must add up
  to AMOUNT exactly.
- `--shares A=2,B=1`: split in proportion.
- `--percent A=60,B=40`: must add up to exactly 100.
- Every name in a split must be a member; duplicates are refused.
- `--currency` defaults to the main currency. Any other currency must have
  a rate set, else refused.
- `--date YYYY-MM-DD` must be a real calendar date in exactly that format;
  default is today's local date.
- `--category` defaults to `other`.
- IDs start at 1, increase by 1, and are never reused after removal.
  `expense remove` of an unknown ID is refused.

### Amounts
- AMOUNT (expenses, payments, `--exact` values) must be a positive number
  with at most two decimals. `12.345` is refused, not rounded. Zero,
  negative, and non-numbers are refused.

### Currency and rates
- `rate set USD 0.92`: one USD = 0.92 main currency. Rate must be a
  positive number. Setting a rate for the main currency is refused.
- An expense or payment is converted with the rate in force when it is
  added; that rate is frozen with it. Later `rate set` affects only things
  added afterwards.
- `base_amount = amount × rate`, rounded to the cent with halves always
  going up (0.125 → 0.13).

### Splitting and cents
- Each person's exact part of `base_amount` is computed, rounded **down** to
  the cent, then the leftover cents go out one each, in order, until none
  remain. Order is the order typed in the option, or join order for
  "everyone".
  - 10.00 among Alice, Bob, Cara → 3.34, 3.33, 3.33.
  - 10.00 with `--shares A=1,B=2` → A 3.34, B 6.66.
- Percent and shares work the same way (exact proportional part, round
  down, leftover cents in listed order).

### Payments
- FROM and TO must be members and must differ. Same amount, currency, date
  rules as expenses.

### Balances
- balance = (sum of `base_amount` of expenses they paid) − (sum of their
  shares) + (payments they sent) − (payments they received), all in base.
  Positive = owed money, negative = owes. Every member listed in join
  order; zero shows as `"0.00"`.

### Settle
- Repeatedly take the person who owes the most and the person owed the
  most; the payment is whatever amount evens out one of them
  (min of the two magnitudes). Ties for "most" are broken alphabetically,
  ignoring case. Payments listed in the order worked out. Nothing to settle
  → `[]`.

### Errors
- Any refusal leaves `kitty.json` exactly as it was, prints
  `error: <message>` to stderr, exits 1.

## Calls I made (owner may override)

- **Description** may be several words without quotes
  (`expense add Alice 45 Dinner at Luigi's`); words are joined with single
  spaces. Options may come before or after it. Empty description refused.
- **Foreign-currency `--exact`:** each person's part of `base_amount` is
  proportional to their exact amount, then the same round-down/leftover
  rule applies. So shares always sum to `base_amount`; for main-currency
  expenses this reproduces the exact amounts.
- **Order of `shares`** in `expense list` is the split order: the order
  typed in the option, or join order for "everyone". It is stored that way.
- **Zero shares:** everyone named in a split (or everyone, for the default)
  is in the expense, even if their rounded share is `0.00` (e.g. 0.01 among
  three). They appear in `shares`, count as "in" the expense for
  `member remove`, get a `history` entry, and appear in `report` for that
  category.
- **Currency codes** are case-insensitive and stored upper-case; they must
  be exactly three letters A–Z. `--currency` equal to the main currency is
  allowed (rate 1).
- **Number formats:** amounts are digits optionally followed by a dot and
  1–2 digits (`45`, `45.5`, `45.50`); no signs, commas, exponents, `nan`,
  `inf`. Rates, `--shares` and `--percent` values are positive decimals of
  any precision. `--exact` values follow the amount rule.
- **Categories** are case-insensitive, stored lower-case, non-empty.
- **History** includes every expense where the person paid or has a share,
  and every payment they sent or received. `change` for an expense is
  (base_amount if they paid, else 0) − their share (may be `"0.00"`). For a
  payment: sender `+amount`, description `"Payment to <TO>"`; receiver
  `−amount`, description `"Payment from <FROM>"`. Sorted by date, then by
  the order things were added (a single global sequence across expenses
  and payments). Running `balance` after each entry; the last equals
  `balances`. Unknown name refused.
- **Report:** `{category: {person: total share}}` using shares, not what
  was paid. Categories alphabetical, only those with expenses; within a
  category, only people with a share in it, in join order.
- **Export:** CSV with header `id,date,payer,description,amount,currency,category,base_amount`,
  one row per expense in ID order, amounts as two-decimal strings;
  overwrites FILE if it exists. Doesn't modify `kitty.json`. Write failure
  is refused with an error.
- **JSON output** uses `ensure_ascii=False` so names like José print
  readably.
- **Corrupt or unreadable `kitty.json`** is refused with an error, not a
  traceback.

## Left to the builder

- Module layout inside `kitty/`, internal storage schema of `kitty.json`
  (store decimals as strings; include a format version, the global
  sequence counter, and the next expense ID), error message wording.
- Tests with stdlib `unittest`, covering every rule above, Sam's examples,
  the cent-rounding cases, and the "file unchanged on refusal" guarantee.

# Kitty: shared trip-cost tracker — design

Date: 2026-11-17
Status: draft for approval

## Intent and why

A group of friends on a trip need to record who paid for what, so that at
the end they know who owes whom and how to even up with as few paybacks as
possible. The owner is not a programmer; their friend Sam writes scripts
and will hook the tool up to a spreadsheet. So the tool is a command-line
program whose reports are machine-readable JSON in exactly the format
below, and which never crashes on bad input: it explains the problem and
stops.

## Goals

- Track members, expenses (with flexible splits and foreign currencies),
  payments between members, and exchange rates.
- Report balances, a settlement plan, per-person history, a per-category
  spending report, and a CSV export.
- Exact money math: shares of an expense always add up to it to the cent.

## Non-goals

- No GUI, no web, no multi-user sync, no editing of an existing expense
  (remove and re-add instead), no automatic exchange-rate lookup.

## Anti-goals (would be a failure even if it "works")

- Needs anything installed beyond the Mac's Python 3.9.6.
- A refused command changes `kitty.json` in any way, or a crash leaves it
  half-written.
- A Python traceback shown to the user for bad input.
- Balances that drift by a cent, or shares that don't sum to the expense.
- Past expenses silently changing when the group or a rate changes.

## Constraints

- Run as `python3 -m kitty <command> ...` from the folder that contains the
  `kitty` package. Python 3.9.6, standard library only (so no `match`, no
  `X | Y` type unions at runtime, `date.fromisoformat` is limited, etc.).
- State lives in `kitty.json` in the **current working directory**.
- Success: exit status 0. Any refusal: one line `error: <message>` on
  stderr, nothing on stdout, exit status 1, `kitty.json` byte-for-byte
  unchanged. This includes command-line usage mistakes (unknown command,
  missing argument, unknown option) — argparse's default exit status 2 must
  be overridden to 1 with the same `error:` format.

## Approaches considered

1. **Plain Python package, stdlib only, JSON file state** — chosen.
   `decimal` for money, `json`, `csv`, `argparse`. Matches every constraint.
2. **SQLite database for state** — rejected: Sam asked for `kitty.json`, and
   a plain JSON file is easier for his scripts.
3. **Third-party libraries (e.g. click, a money library) or another
   language** — rejected: violates "nothing to install" and
   `python3 -m kitty`.

The owner agreed to approach 1.

## Commands and output

All JSON output is printed with Python's default `json.dumps` separators
(`", "` and `": "`), on one line, as in the examples. Money is always a
string with exactly two decimals. Money is in the main (base) currency,
except an expense's own `amount`. Object key order is significant and is
given below.

| Command | Prints on success |
|---|---|
| `init CUR` | nothing |
| `member add NAME` / `member remove NAME` | nothing |
| `member list` | `["Alice", "Bob"]` — join order |
| `expense add PAYER AMOUNT DESCRIPTION [opts]` | the new ID, e.g. `1` |
| `expense list` | list of expense objects, by ID |
| `expense remove ID` | nothing |
| `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT [--currency C] [--date D]` | nothing |
| `rate set CUR RATE` | nothing |
| `balances` | object, members in join order |
| `settle` | list of payments, in the order computed |
| `history NAME` | list of entries |
| `report` | object of objects |
| `export FILE` | nothing (writes the CSV) |

Examples (from Sam):

- `expense list`: `[{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice", "description": "Dinner", "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD", "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food", "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}]`
- `balances`: `{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}`
- `settle`: `[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]`
- `history Bob`: `[{"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner", "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}]`
- `report`: `{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}`

Empty results print `[]` or `{}`.

## Rules decided with the owner

### Kitty and state
- `init CUR` creates `kitty.json` with CUR as the main currency. Refused if
  `kitty.json` already exists. Every other command is refused if it doesn't.
- Anything that changes state is fully validated first; the file is saved
  only on success, by writing a temp file in the same folder and
  `os.replace`-ing it over `kitty.json`.

### Members
- Names are case-insensitive for matching everywhere (in every command and
  option), but always displayed as first added. Adding a name that matches
  an existing one case-insensitively is refused.
- Names may not contain `,` or `=`. (Builder's call: also refuse empty or
  all-whitespace names; strip surrounding whitespace.)
- `member remove` is refused if the person appears in any expense (as payer
  or in its shares) or any payment (as sender or receiver). Otherwise it
  succeeds. Unknown name is refused.

### Expenses
- PAYER must be a member. The payer need not be among the people sharing.
- "Everyone" (no split option) means the members at the moment the expense
  is added; the computed shares are stored with the expense and never
  recomputed. Later joiners are not included in earlier expenses.
- At most one of `--among`, `--exact`, `--shares`, `--percent`.
- `--among A,B`: equal split among those named.
- `--exact A=30,B=20`: amounts in the expense's own currency; must add up
  to AMOUNT exactly.
- `--shares A=2,B=1`: split in proportion.
- `--percent A=60,B=40`: must add up to exactly 100.
- Every name in a split must be a member; duplicates are refused.
- `--currency` defaults to the main currency. Any other currency must have
  a rate set, else refused.
- `--date YYYY-MM-DD` must be a real calendar date in exactly that format;
  default is today's local date.
- `--category` defaults to `other`.
- IDs start at 1, increase by 1, and are never reused after removal.
  `expense remove` of an unknown ID is refused.

### Amounts
- AMOUNT (expenses, payments, `--exact` values) must be a positive number
  with at most two decimals. `12.345` is refused, not rounded. Zero,
  negative, and non-numbers are refused.

### Currency and rates
- `rate set USD 0.92`: one USD = 0.92 main currency. Rate must be a
  positive number. Setting a rate for the main currency is refused.
- An expense or payment is converted with the rate in force when it is
  added; that rate is frozen with it. Later `rate set` affects only things
  added afterwards.
- `base_amount = amount × rate`, rounded to the cent with halves always
  going up (0.125 → 0.13).

### Splitting and cents
- Each person's exact part of `base_amount` is computed, rounded **down** to
  the cent, then the leftover cents go out one each, in order, until none
  remain. Order is the order typed in the option, or join order for
  "everyone".
  - 10.00 among Alice, Bob, Cara → 3.34, 3.33, 3.33.
  - 10.00 with `--shares A=1,B=2` → A 3.34, B 6.66.
- Percent and shares work the same way (exact proportional part, round
  down, leftover cents in listed order).

### Payments
- FROM and TO must be members and must differ. Same amount, currency, date
  rules as expenses.

### Balances
- balance = (sum of `base_amount` of expenses they paid) − (sum of their
  shares) + (payments they sent) − (payments they received), all in base.
  Positive = owed money, negative = owes. Every member listed in join
  order; zero shows as `"0.00"`.

### Settle
- Repeatedly take the person who owes the most and the person owed the
  most; the payment is whatever amount evens out one of them
  (min of the two magnitudes). Ties for "most" are broken alphabetically,
  ignoring case. Payments listed in the order worked out. Nothing to settle
  → `[]`.

### Errors
- Any refusal leaves `kitty.json` exactly as it was, prints
  `error: <message>` to stderr, exits 1.

## Calls I made (owner may override)

- **Description** may be several words without quotes
  (`expense add Alice 45 Dinner at Luigi's`); words are joined with single
  spaces. Options may come before or after it. Empty description refused.
- **Foreign-currency `--exact`:** each person's part of `base_amount` is
  proportional to their exact amount, then the same round-down/leftover
  rule applies. So shares always sum to `base_amount`; for main-currency
  expenses this reproduces the exact amounts.
- **Order of `shares`** in `expense list` is the split order: the order
  typed in the option, or join order for "everyone". It is stored that way.
- **Zero shares:** everyone named in a split (or everyone, for the default)
  is in the expense, even if their rounded share is `0.00` (e.g. 0.01 among
  three). They appear in `shares`, count as "in" the expense for
  `member remove`, get a `history` entry, and appear in `report` for that
  category.
- **Currency codes** are case-insensitive and stored upper-case; they must
  be exactly three letters A–Z. `--currency` equal to the main currency is
  allowed (rate 1).
- **Number formats:** amounts are digits optionally followed by a dot and
  1–2 digits (`45`, `45.5`, `45.50`); no signs, commas, exponents, `nan`,
  `inf`. Rates, `--shares` and `--percent` values are positive decimals of
  any precision. `--exact` values follow the amount rule.
- **Categories** are case-insensitive, stored lower-case, non-empty.
- **History** includes every expense where the person paid or has a share,
  and every payment they sent or received. `change` for an expense is
  (base_amount if they paid, else 0) − their share (may be `"0.00"`). For a
  payment: sender `+amount`, description `"Payment to <TO>"`; receiver
  `−amount`, description `"Payment from <FROM>"`. Sorted by date, then by
  the order things were added (a single global sequence across expenses
  and payments). Running `balance` after each entry; the last equals
  `balances`. Unknown name refused.
- **Report:** `{category: {person: total share}}` using shares, not what
  was paid. Categories alphabetical, only those with expenses; within a
  category, only people with a share in it, in join order.
- **Export:** CSV with header `id,date,payer,description,amount,currency,category,base_amount`,
  one row per expense in ID order, amounts as two-decimal strings;
  overwrites FILE if it exists. Doesn't modify `kitty.json`. Write failure
  is refused with an error.
- **JSON output** uses `ensure_ascii=False` so names like José print
  readably.
- **Corrupt or unreadable `kitty.json`** is refused with an error, not a
  traceback.

## Left to the builder

- Module layout inside `kitty/`, internal storage schema of `kitty.json`
  (store decimals as strings; include a format version, the global
  sequence counter, and the next expense ID), error message wording.
- Tests with stdlib `unittest`, covering every rule above, Sam's examples,
  the cent-rounding cases, and the "file unchanged on refusal" guarantee.

import os
import re
import stat
import tempfile
from decimal import Decimal

from kitty.errors import KittyError
from kitty.money import parse_currency, parse_date

STATE_FILE = "kitty.json"

_KEYS = ("version", "base_currency", "members", "rates", "next_id",
         "next_seq", "expenses", "payments")
_EXPENSE_KEYS = ("id", "seq", "date", "payer", "description", "amount",
                 "currency", "rate", "base_amount", "category", "shares")
_PAYMENT_KEYS = ("seq", "date", "from", "to", "amount", "currency", "rate",
                 "base_amount")

_CODE = re.compile(r"[A-Z]{3}", re.ASCII)
_AMOUNT = re.compile(r"\d{1,12}\.\d{2}", re.ASCII)
# a base amount is at most (12-digit amount) x (12-integer-digit rate)
_BASE = re.compile(r"\d{1,24}\.\d{2}", re.ASCII)
_RATE = re.compile(r"\d{1,12}(\.\d{1,28})?", re.ASCII)


def new_state(base_currency):
    return {
        "version": 1,
        "base_currency": parse_currency(base_currency),
        "members": [],
        "rates": {},
        "next_id": 1,
        "next_seq": 1,
        "expenses": [],
        "payments": [],
    }


def init(path, base_currency):
    if os.path.exists(path):
        raise KittyError("%s already exists" % path)
    save(path, new_state(base_currency))


def _reject_constant(name):
    raise ValueError("%s is not allowed" % name)


def load(path):
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            state = json.load(f, parse_constant=_reject_constant)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise KittyError("%s not found; run `init` first" % path)
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError("cannot read %s: %s" % (path, e))
    except (ValueError, RecursionError) as e:
        raise KittyError("%s is corrupt: not valid JSON: %s" % (path, e))
    try:
        validate(state)
    except _Bad as e:
        raise KittyError("%s is corrupt: %s" % (path, e))
    return state


class _Bad(Exception):
    """A problem in the stored state; str(e) says where."""


def _need(ok, where, what):
    if not ok:
        raise _Bad("%s: %s" % (where, what))


def _is_int(v):
    return isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool)


def _matches(pattern, v):
    return isinstance(v, str) and pattern.fullmatch(v) is not None


def _text(v):
    return isinstance(v, str) and v != "" and v == v.strip()


def _check_keys(obj, keys, where):
    _need(isinstance(obj, dict), where, "must be an object")
    missing = [k for k in keys if k not in obj]
    _need(not missing, where, "missing " + ", ".join(missing))


def _check_date(v, where):
    _need(isinstance(v, str), where, "must be a YYYY-MM-DD date")
    try:
        parse_date(v)
    except KittyError:
        _need(False, where, "must be a real YYYY-MM-DD date")


def _check_seq(v, where, state, seqs):
    _need(_is_int(v) and 1 <= v < state["next_seq"], where,
          "must be a whole number from 1 to next_seq - 1")
    _need(v not in seqs, where, "duplicate sequence number %d" % v)
    seqs.add(v)


def _check_money_fields(obj, where):
    _need(_matches(_AMOUNT, obj["amount"]) and Decimal(obj["amount"]) > 0,
          where + ".amount", "must be a positive two-decimal string")
    _need(_matches(_CODE, obj["currency"]), where + ".currency",
          "must be a 3-letter upper-case code")
    _need(_matches(_RATE, obj["rate"]) and Decimal(obj["rate"]) > 0,
          where + ".rate", "must be a positive decimal string")
    _need(_matches(_BASE, obj["base_amount"]) and Decimal(obj["base_amount"]) > 0,
          where + ".base_amount", "must be a positive two-decimal string")


def validate(state):
    """Raise _Bad unless state has exactly the shape kitty writes."""
    if not isinstance(state, dict):
        raise _Bad("expected a JSON object")
    missing = [k for k in _KEYS if k not in state]
    if missing:
        raise _Bad("missing " + ", ".join(missing))
    _need(_is_int(state["version"]) and state["version"] == 1, "version", "must be 1")
    base = state["base_currency"]
    _need(_matches(_CODE, base), "base_currency", "must be a 3-letter upper-case code")

    members = state["members"]
    _need(isinstance(members, list), "members", "must be a list")
    keys = set()
    for i, m in enumerate(members):
        where = "members[%d]" % i
        _need(_text(m) and "," not in m and "=" not in m, where,
              "must be a non-empty name without ',' or '='")
        _need(m.casefold() not in keys, where, "duplicate name %s" % m)
        keys.add(m.casefold())
    names = set(members)

    rates = state["rates"]
    _need(isinstance(rates, dict), "rates", "must be an object")
    for cur, rate in rates.items():
        where = "rates.%s" % cur
        _need(_matches(_CODE, cur), where, "must be a 3-letter upper-case code")
        _need(cur != base, where, "cannot have a rate for the base currency")
        _need(_matches(_RATE, rate) and Decimal(rate) > 0, where,
              "must be a positive decimal string")

    for key in ("next_id", "next_seq"):
        _need(_is_int(state[key]) and state[key] >= 1, key, "must be a whole number >= 1")

    seqs = set()
    ids = set()
    expenses = state["expenses"]
    _need(isinstance(expenses, list), "expenses", "must be a list")
    for i, e in enumerate(expenses):
        where = "expenses[%d]" % i
        _check_keys(e, _EXPENSE_KEYS, where)
        _need(_is_int(e["id"]) and 1 <= e["id"] < state["next_id"], where + ".id",
              "must be a whole number from 1 to next_id - 1")
        _need(e["id"] not in ids, where + ".id", "duplicate id %d" % e["id"])
        ids.add(e["id"])
        _check_seq(e["seq"], where + ".seq", state, seqs)
        _check_date(e["date"], where + ".date")
        _need(isinstance(e["payer"], str) and e["payer"] in names, where + ".payer",
              "must be a member")
        _need(_text(e["description"]), where + ".description", "must be non-empty text")
        _need(_text(e["category"]) and e["category"] == e["category"].lower(),
              where + ".category", "must be non-empty lower-case text")
        _check_money_fields(e, where)
        shares = e["shares"]
        _need(isinstance(shares, dict) and shares, where + ".shares",
              "must be a non-empty object")
        for name, share in shares.items():
            _need(name in names, where + ".shares", "%s is not a member" % name)
            _need(_matches(_BASE, share), where + ".shares." + name,
                  "must be a two-decimal string")

    payments = state["payments"]
    _need(isinstance(payments, list), "payments", "must be a list")
    for i, p in enumerate(payments):
        where = "payments[%d]" % i
        _check_keys(p, _PAYMENT_KEYS, where)
        _check_seq(p["seq"], where + ".seq", state, seqs)
        _check_date(p["date"], where + ".date")
        for key in ("from", "to"):
            _need(isinstance(p[key], str) and p[key] in names, where + "." + key,
                  "must be a member")
        _need(p["from"] != p["to"], where, "from and to must differ")
        _check_money_fields(p, where)


def write_atomically(path, write, newline=None):
    """Write a file via a temp file in the same folder and os.replace.

    write(f) produces the content. The result keeps the mode of the file it
    replaces, or gets 0644 if new. On any failure the temp file is removed
    and the original is untouched; OSError becomes a KittyError.
    """
    folder = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    tmp_name = None
    try:
        try:
            mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(path).st_mode)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            mode = 0o644
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
                "w", encoding="utf-8", newline=newline, dir=folder,
                prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".tmp", delete=False) as tmp:
            tmp_name = tmp.name
            write(tmp)
            tmp.flush()
            os.fchmod(tmp.fileno(), mode)
            os.fsync(tmp.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_name, path)
    except BaseException as e:
        if tmp_name is not None:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp_name)
            except OSError:
                pass
        if isinstance(e, OSError):
            raise KittyError("cannot write %s: %s" % (path, e))
        raise


def save(path, state):
    def write(f):
        json.dump(state, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
        f.write("\n")
    write_atomically(path, write)

I've added `expense edit ID` and `--in CUR` for `balances` and `settle`. All 91 tests pass: the 74 that were already there and 17 new ones. Nothing is committed yet.

**`expense edit ID`**
- It takes the options you listed and changes only what you give. The expense keeps its ID and its place in `history`. A refused edit leaves `kitty.json` exactly as it was, like every other command.
- If the amount or currency changes and you don't give a split option, it's split equally among the same people as before. That includes expenses that were first split with `--shares` or `--percent`.
- A split option on its own re-splits the current amount. `--exact` has to add up to the new amount, in the new currency.
- `--description` takes a single value, so a description with several words needs quotes: `--description "Dinner at Luigi's"`.

**`balances --in CUR` / `settle --in CUR`**
- Each amount is converted at CUR's current rate and rounded to the cent, in the same JSON as now.
- A currency with no rate, or a code that isn't three letters, is an error. The base currency shows the usual amounts.
- `settle` works out the payments in the base currency as before, then converts each amount.
- Because each amount is rounded separately, converted balances can be a cent off from adding up to zero. I noted this in the README.

**Choices I made where your request didn't say:**
- **Amount changes, same currency:** if only the amount changes, the expense keeps the rate it already had rather than today's rate. This keeps the existing rule that a later `rate set` doesn't change past expenses. Giving `--currency` with the currency it already has counts as no change.
- **Edit with no options:** `expense edit 3` with nothing to change is refused with an error.
- **Tiny converted payments:** in a currency worth much more than the base, a one-cent `settle` payment can convert to `"0.00"`. I left those lines in rather than hide a payment.

I updated the README. The design doc in `docs/superpowers/specs/` still lists "no editing of an existing expense" as a non-goal, and I didn't change it. The changes are in `kitty/ledger.py`, `kitty/reports.py` and `kitty/cli.py`, and the new tests are mostly in `tests/test_ledger_edit.py`.
